column1: # Sigma detection validation manifest — TAB-separated. Paths are repo-root-relative.
# The SIXTH column is the true-negative fixture ('-' for none) and it is what makes a
# rule's filter_* blocks provable. A TP row can only show that a rule FIRES; it can never
# show that an exclusion still works, so a filter that silently stopped matching would
# keep this gate green while the rule quietly went noisy. Where a row names a TN, the rule
# must ALSO stay silent on it, and a zircolite ERROR is failed rather than counted as
# silence (see run-sigma-validation.sh for that three-way contract).
# A TN fixture is a NEAR-MISS, not unrelated traffic: same event id and channel as the TP,
# one thing changed so that exactly one filter_* block catches it. For the correlation
# rules it is also sized PAST the threshold (101 objects for SharpHound's gte-100, 205
# files for the Sysmon-11 gte-200), so if the filter broke the rule really would fire and
# the row really would go red. A TN that merely falls under the threshold proves nothing.
# Rules that carry a filter_* block but no TN are reported by the runner as an advisory.
# Each row: run the fixture (a JSON-lines event log) through the REAL shipped Sigma rule
# with zircolite (native Sigma via the given pysigma pipeline), and assert the rule's id
# appears in the detections — i.e. the rule fired on the attack telemetry it claims to
# catch. Fixtures live in sigma-fixtures/ (committed JSONL — reviewable, deterministic).
# Covers single-selection, filtered, and value_count-correlation shapes across the
# windows-audit and sysmon pysigma pipelines, plus cloud/SaaS rules with pipeline=none
# (no pysigma pipeline — they have no EventID and match raw field names).
# Cloud/SaaS rules (pipeline=none: no EventID, match raw field names). Only the 20
# flat-field cloud rules run here. Products with dotted/nested field names (GCP, Cloudflare,
# GitLab, Kubernetes, Harbor, Snowflake, Terraform, Vault, …) — plus any otherwise-flat rule
# that keys on an underscored field the flattener strips (e.g. gws_illicit_oauth_grant on
# client_id) — are validated on the nested-field cloud plane instead — zircolite's flattener
